result.topic_en: Using hypergeometric series to determine the coefficients A^(n) of the Fourier cosine expansion of 1/sqrt(a^2+a'^2-2aa' cos phi) (Laplace coefficients), deriving a three-term recurrence among them and a continued-fraction form for their ratios.
result.transcription:
Mit Hülfe des vorhergehenden hat man nun auch sofort
das Nöthige zur Bestimmung der Coëfficienten der Reihe, in
welche $\frac{1}{\sqrt{(aa+a'a'-2aa'\cos\varphi)}}$ entwickelt wird. Setzt man dieselbe
$T = A^0 + 2A'\cos\varphi + 2A''\cos 2\varphi + 2A'''\cos 3\varphi$ u. s. w. so wird, $f$
statt $\frac{a}{a'}$ geschrieben und $r$ statt $\cos\varphi + i\sin\varphi$
$\frac{1}{a'}(1-fr)^{-\frac12}(1-fr^{-1})^{-\frac12} = T$ also
[42] $a'A^0 = 1 + \frac{1.1}{2.2}ff + \frac{1.1.3.3}{2.2.4.4}f^4 + \frac{1.1.3.3.5.5}{2.2.4.4.6.6}f^6 \ldots = F(\frac12,\frac12,1,ff)$
$a'A' = \frac12 f(1 + \frac{1.3}{2.4}ff + \frac{1.3.3.5}{2.4.4.6}f^4 + \frac{1.3.3.5.5.7}{2.4.4.6.6.8}f^6\ldots) = \frac12 f.F(\frac12,\frac32,2,f^2)$
$a'A'' = \frac12\cdot\frac34 ff(1 + \frac{1.5}{2.6}ff + \frac{1.5.3.7}{2.6.4.8}f^4 + \frac{1.5.3.7.5.9}{2.6.4.8.6.10}f^6\ldots) = \frac{1.3}{2.4}ff.F(\frac12,\frac52,3,ff)$
$a'A''' = \frac{1.3.5}{2.4.6}f^3(1 + \frac{1.7}{2.8}ff + \frac{1.7.3.9}{2.8.4.10}f^4 + \frac{1.7.3.9.5.11}{2.8.4.10.6.12}f^8\ldots) = \frac{1.3.5}{2.4.6}f^3 F(\frac12,\frac72,4,ff)$
u. s. w.
Aus der Verbindung der Gleichungen 15 und 19 folgt
$\beta(\alpha-\gamma)x F(\alpha,\beta+1,\gamma+1) - \gamma(\gamma-1)F(\alpha,\beta-1,\gamma-1) + \gamma(\gamma-1+(\beta-\alpha)x)F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) = 0$
Als für unsern Fall, wo $\alpha=\frac12$, $\beta=\gamma-\frac12$
$-(\gamma-\frac12)^2 x F(\frac12,\gamma+\frac12,\gamma+1) - \gamma(\gamma-1)F(\frac12,\gamma-\frac32,\gamma-1) + \gamma(\gamma-1+(\gamma-1)x)F(\frac12,\gamma-\frac12,\gamma)$
Es ist folglich weil
$ffA^{(\gamma-2)}, fA^{(\gamma-1)}, A^{(\gamma)}$ proportional sind
$\gamma(\gamma-1)F(\frac12,\gamma-\frac32,\gamma-1)$, $(\gamma-\frac32)\gamma F(\frac12,\gamma-\frac12,\gamma)$, $(\gamma-\frac32)(\gamma-\frac12)F(\frac12,\gamma+\frac12,\gamma+1)$
und
[43] $(\gamma-\frac32)A^{(\gamma-2)} - (\gamma-1)(f+\frac1f)A^{(\gamma-1)} + (\gamma-\frac12)A^{(\gamma)} = 0$
also
$A^{(0)} - 2(f+\frac1f)A' + 3A'' = 0$
$3A' - 4(f+\frac1f)A'' + 5A''' = 0$
$5A'' - 6(f+\frac1f)A''' + 7A'''' = 0$ etc.
Man setze
[44] $\frac21\cdot\frac{1+ff}{f}\cdot\frac{A'}{A^0} = B^0$, $\frac43\cdot\frac{1+ff}{f}\cdot\frac{A''}{A'} = B'$, $\frac65\cdot\frac{1+ff}{f}\cdot\frac{A'''}{A''} = B''$ so ist
so wird
[45] $B^0 = \frac{1}{1-\frac98(\frac{f}{1+ff})^2 B'}$, $B' = \frac{1}{1-\frac{25}{24}(\frac{f}{1+ff})^2 B''}$, $B'' = \frac{1}{1-\frac{49}{48}(\frac{f}{1+ff})^2 B'''}$ etc.

methods.what: Generating-function expression of the expansion via r = e^{i phi}
Laplace coefficients expressed as hypergeometric series
Contiguous relation for the hypergeometric function from combining equations 15 and 19
Three-term recurrence for the coefficients A^(n)
Continued-fraction representation of ratios of successive coefficients
